title: Client Intake and Conflict Check Policy
text:
1. The intake coordinator enters the client name, the counterparty names and the marks/patents involved in the conflict system.
2. The system checks existing clients, adverse parties and the firm's watch database.
3. The result must be cleared by the Risk and Compliance Officer within **1 working day**.
4. If a potential conflict is found, the matter is escalated to the **Managing Partner**, who decides whether to decline or to seek informed written consent from both clients.

title: Trademark Search and Clearance
text:
- **Knock-out search**: identical and near-identical marks only, in the requested classes. Delivered within **1 working day**. Fee: **IDR 750,000 per class**.
- **Comprehensive search**: identical, phonetic, visual and conceptual similarity, including related classes and pending applications in the DJKI database. Delivered within **3 working days**. Fee: **IDR 2,000,000 per class**.
- **Device (logo) search**: added to a comprehensive search when the mark contains a figurative element, using Vienna classification codes. Surcharge: **IDR 1,000,000 per class**.

title: Trademark Search and Clearance
text:
1. The associate confirms the exact mark, the goods/services and the Nice classes with the client.
2. The paralegal runs the search on the DJKI public database and the firm's internal watch database.
3. Each conflicting mark is rated **Low, Medium or High risk** using the Similarity Matrix (Annex A).
4. A senior associate reviews every High-risk finding before the opinion is sent.
5. The clearance opinion is issued on the standard template (TMPL-TM-SRCH) and saved in the matter folder.

title: Domestic Trademark Filing
text:

title: Responding to Substantive Refusals (Office Actions)
text: How the firm handles a provisional refusal issued by the DJKI examiner during substantive examination.

How the firm handles a provisional refusal issued by the DJKI examiner during substantive examination.

title: Responding to Substantive Refusals (Office Actions)
text:
- The official deadline to respond to a provisional refusal is **30 days** from the date of the notice.
- Internal rule: the client must be reported to within **2 working days** of receipt, and the draft response must be ready **7 calendar days** before the official deadline.
- Every deadline is entered in the docketing system with reminders at **14, 7 and 3 days** before the due date.

title: Responding to Substantive Refusals (Office Actions)
text:

title: Trademark Opposition (Keberatan) Procedure
section: 1. Filing an Opposition for a Client
text:
- Oppositions must be filed during the **2-month publication period**.
- The watch service team sends a watch notice to the client within **3 working days** of spotting a potentially conflicting publication.
- Client instructions must be received at least **10 working days** before the end of the publication period. Later instructions are treated as urgent.
- Required evidence: proof of prior rights, evidence of use or reputation, and the signed Power of Attorney.
- Professional fee: **IDR 6,500,000** per opposition, excluding official fees and translation costs.

title: Trademark Renewal and Docketing
text: An Indonesian trademark registration lasts **10 years** and may be renewed for the same period. A renewal may be filed within **6 months before** the expiry date, and late renewal is possible up to **6 months after** expiry with an additional official fine.

title: Trademark Renewal and Docketing
text: The docketing system sends renewal reminders to the client at **12 months, 6 months, 3 months and 1 month** before expiry. After expiry, a final grace-period reminder is sent every **30 days** until the grace period ends.

title: Trademark Renewal and Docketing
text:
1. The docketing team verifies the registration details and the current owner name.
2. If the owner name or address has changed, a recordal of change is filed **before or together with** the renewal.
3. The associate files the renewal and reports the filing receipt within **1 working day**.

title: Madrid Protocol Filings (Outgoing and Incoming)
text:
- Indonesian clients may file an international application through DJKI as the Office of origin, based on an Indonesian application or registration.
- Internal timeline: the draft MM2 form is prepared within **3 working days** of receiving complete instructions.
- Professional fee: **IDR 5,000,000** per international application, plus **IDR 750,000** per designated country. WIPO fees are passed through at cost.
- The associate must remind the client that, for **5 years** from the international registration date, the international registration depends on the basic Indonesian mark (central attack).
